title: Why rain does not end a drought at once
titleZh: 下雨为何不等于旱情立刻结束
summaryZh: 英格兰部分地区的水务公司在保护供水的同时，需要持续降雨补充水库。

sentences.text: On 20 October 2026, the government reported on a meeting with water company leaders about drought in England.
sentences.zh: 2026年10月20日，政府报道了与水务公司负责人讨论英格兰旱情的一次会议。

sentences.text: Parts of the South East and South West had experienced their driest April-to-September period in more than a century.
sentences.zh: 英格兰东南部和西南部的一些地区经历了一个多世纪以来最干旱的4月至9月。

sentences.text: Reservoir levels were low, and severe drought had been declared in parts of six counties the previous week.
sentences.zh: 水库水位很低，前一周已有六个郡的部分地区宣布进入严重干旱状态。

sentences.text: However, public water supplies were still continuing when the report was published.
sentences.zh: 不过，在报道发表时，公共供水仍在持续。

sentences.text: The declaration allowed extra steps to protect supplies before a possible interruption, rather than announcing that taps had already stopped working.
sentences.zh: 宣布严重干旱使有关方面能在可能停供之前采取额外保护措施，而不是宣布水龙头已经断水。

sentences.text: Companies were checking reservoir and river levels every day and improving checks on water quality.
sentences.zh: 水务公司每天检查水库及河流水位，并加强水质检查。

sentences.text: They were also finding leaks more quickly and moving water through their networks towards areas with the lowest reservoirs.
sentences.zh: 它们还在更快地寻找漏水点，并通过管网把水调往水库水位最低的地区。

sentences.text: Where appropriate, they were reducing water pressure at night to help protect supplies.
sentences.zh: 在适宜的地方，它们正在夜间降低水压，以帮助保障供水。

sentences.text: The Environment Agency had allowed two companies to release less water from certain reservoirs into local rivers.
sentences.zh: 英国环境署已允许两家公司减少从特定水库向当地河流放水。

sentences.text: Other requests, including possible restrictions on non-essential business use, were still being considered.
sentences.zh: 其他申请，包括可能限制非必要商业用水的申请，仍在审议中。

sentences.text: Fish rescue plans were also being prepared in case falling reservoir levels made action necessary.
sentences.zh: 有关方面也在准备鱼类救援计划，以防水库水位继续下降而需要采取行动。

sentences.text: These were preparations, not a statement that every planned measure had already begun.
sentences.zh: 这些是准备工作，并不表示每项计划中的措施都已开始。

sentences.text: Rain was expected later that week, but the Environment Agency said a longer period of wet weather was needed.
sentences.zh: 预计那一周晚些时候会下雨，但英国环境署表示需要更长时间的湿润天气。

sentences.text: It estimated that rainfall over the following six months needed to reach at least 120 percent of the average for the country to be considered out of drought by early spring.
sentences.zh: 该机构估计，要到初春时认定英格兰已摆脱干旱，接下来六个月的降雨量需要达到平均水平的至少120%。

sentences.text: This explains why a rainy day and a recovered water supply system are not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这说明了为什么下雨的一天与供水系统恢复并不是一回事。

sentences.text: The group asked people to use water wisely in the weeks and months ahead, while companies remained responsible for maintaining public supplies.
sentences.zh: 该工作组呼吁人们在接下来几周和几个月里明智用水，而保障公共供水的责任仍由水务公司承担。

words.note: had been declared为过去完成时被动，指正式宣布旱情。
leaks是漏水处的复数，不是账单、阀门或水表。
water pressure指水压，降低水压不等于降低水价、水温或水质。
being prepared表示正在准备计划，尚不能说计划已执行或取消。
responsible for表示对某项职责负责。

phrases.note: 过去进行时被动表达当时未完成的审议。

sentences.note: rather than明确区分预防措施与已经发生的停水。

questions.text: How can a community save water without shifting all responsibility to households?
questions.zh: 社区怎样节水，同时不把全部责任转给家庭？

expressions.text: A short-term improvement does not mean…
expressions.note: 可复用教学表达，不是原文引语。
